summary: The Tax Exempt Hospital Transparency Act requires tax-exempt hospital organizations to submit additional detailed information to the Internal Revenue Service on their annual tax returns. It creates tiered reporting rules based on the size and revenue of the hospitals, setting specific requirements for large and high-revenue facilities regarding health needs, spending, services, advertising, and the federal 340B drug discount program. Additionally, the bill directs the Government Accountability Office to conduct a study on administrative compliance costs and to estimate potential tax revenue from the top 25 highest-revenue tax-exempt hospitals.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with new, expanded annual reporting requirements on their IRS returns, providing detailed financial, operational, clinical, and community benefit data, with specialized reporting tiers for large and high-revenue entities.
Must separately report facility-level data and detailed metrics on top community health needs, quality improvement spending, and nonclinical programming costs.
Must separately report facility-level data, advertising costs, service line revenues and expenses mapped to a standardized taxonomy, and detailed metrics under the Federal 340B drug discount program.
Must initiate a study and report to congressional committees on the administrative and compliance costs of the new rules and estimate tax potentials for top-revenue hospital organizations.

key_provisions: Requires all tax-exempt hospital organizations to include on their annual IRS Form 990 a description of how they address community health needs, audited financial statements, a CMS certification number, the cost value of financial assistance provided, and counts of financial assistance applications received, granted, and denied.

Imposes additional reporting on large tax-exempt hospital organizations (those with more than 100 staffed beds and not categorized as critical access or rural emergency hospitals), requiring them to report spending and impacts for their top three health needs, as well as spending on quality improvement, nonclinical programming, and other community benefits.

Imposes additional reporting on high-revenue tax-exempt hospital organizations (those with net patient revenue over $100,000,000), requiring details on allowable and unallowable advertising costs, health service line revenues and costs, and specific information concerning the federal 340B drug discount program.

Mandates that the Department of Health and Human Services publish and maintain a standardized health service line taxonomy that high-revenue hospitals must use to map their internal clinical service lines.

Requires the Government Accountability Office to study the costs imposed on the Treasury and hospitals by these new reporting requirements, and estimate tax revenues for the 25 tax-exempt hospitals with the highest gross revenue if they lacked tax-exempt status.
missing_information: The specific legislative timeline or fiscal year for when the bill would take effect beyond the general conditional effective dates tied to the standardized health service line taxonomy.
The exact monetary value of the compliance costs for hospitals or the Treasury, which are deferred to a future GAO study.
The precise dollar amount of potential tax revenue for the top 25 high-revenue hospitals, which is also deferred to the GAO study.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Tax Exempt Hospital Transparency Act requires tax-exempt hospital organizations to submit additional detailed information to the Internal Revenue Service on their annual tax returns. It creates tiered reporting rules based on the size and revenue of the hospitals, setting specific requirements for large and high-revenue facilities regarding health needs, spending, services, advertising, and the federal 340B drug discount program. Additionally, the bill directs the Government Accountability Office to conduct a study on administrative compliance costs and to estimate potential tax revenue from the top 25 highest-revenue tax-exempt hospitals.
summary_detail.significance: The bill increases federal oversight and transparency for tax-exempt hospitals by mandating extensive new disclosures regarding finances, operational spending, community benefit programs, and drug discount participation. Its impact is centered on tax-exempt hospitals, which must adapt their accounting and reporting procedures to meet the new statutory standards, and federal agencies tasked with coordinating and studying these disclosures.
